messages:
elaine: Heads up — SAST just flagged a HIGH in core-api on main (auth deserialization). Blocking 2.3.0 rollout until triage. Need someone to own and we also need audit logs for any KMS activity around the window.

scan-bot: Auto-scan results uploaded: 1 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM. SARIF: https://scans.internal.redwood/sarif/1732000001. Summary: insecure-deserialize usage in pkg/auth/decoder.go:45 (rule ID: R-ISD-001).

nina: I can take triage. Which PR/build showed it? any repro steps?

elaine: It surfaced in the release branch build: build/2024-11-02-16. Failing job: sast-main. No PR yet, artifact attached in SARIF.

nina: grabbing the SARIF now. quick grep from the repo shows: 
```
$ grep -n "gob.Decode" -R pkg/ || true
pkg/auth/decoder.go:45: decoder.Decode(&claims) // TODO: unsafe, untrusted input
```
I can patch to add schema validation + replace with json.Unmarshal + whitelist. Opening a draft PR.

raj: Security note: marking CVSS ~7.5. For release gating we must treat HIGH findings as blockers unless there is a compensating control. Two asks: 1) update CI so high severity fails the pipeline automatically; 2) capture audit/tracing of any KMS key usage around the window and attach to the ticket. If KMS keys were used by the vulnerable code path, we may need to rotate keys.

omar: For the audit logs: you can query Cloud Logging with this filter to find KMS CryptoKey access around the time: 
```
resource.type="k8s_cluster" AND protoPayload.methodName:("google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" OR "Encrypt") AND timestamp>="2024-11-02T02:30:00Z" AND timestamp<="2024-11-02T04:30:00Z"
```
That will show which service account invoked KMS and the request metadata. I can run the query if you want.

nina: @omar please run the query and paste results here; I want to see whether auth service actually called KMS in that window.

omar: Ran it — see two decrypt calls from svc-auth@redwood-prod. Full entries forwarded to sec-logs bucket: gs://sec-logs/kms-access/2024-11-02/1732000001-kms.json.

raj: Good. Next steps from sec: 1) nina to push fix and tests; 2) infra (omar) to scope KMS usage and determine if key rotation needed; 3) I will open SEC-4521 triage ticket and hold release as P1 until confirmed. Also add audit artifacts to the ticket.

nina: Creating PR now. Patch replaces unsafe decoder and adds unit+fuzz tests. Draft: https://git.internal.redwood/core-api/pull/4812 (opened at 1732000300). CI run shows SAST now clean for that path locally.

alice-oncall: Incident tracker: INCIDENT-4521 created and linked to PR. Tagging oncall for visibility. @eng-oncall please monitor for any anomalies post-deploy. :rotating_light:

scan-bot: CI policy updated by nina: sast-gate now configured with fail_on: [HIGH]. Workflow path: .github/workflows/sast.yml diff in PR.

raj: Once PR is merged, we still require: attach KMS access export to SEC-4521, confirm no exfiltration, and schedule a KMS rotation if the key was invoked by the vulnerable flow. If rotation is needed, coordinate with infra to schedule a short maintenance window.

nina: PR merged at 1732000360. Added mitigation + test + changelog. I attached the SARIF and unit test output to SEC-4521.

omar: Confirmed no suspicious external IPs in the KMS requests; calls originate from internal svc-auth only. Rotation not required for now, but recommend key re-encryption and a follow-up audit in 7 days.

elaine: Thanks everyone. Holding release for 1 hour for final sec sign-off, then proceed if no other issues. Good work. :thumbsup:
